children: *TPG-Backed Asia OneHealthcare Files Prospectus for Malaysia IPO
*Asia OneHealthcare Plans to Sell Up to 4.38B Shares in IPO
TPG-Backed Asia OneHealthcare Files IPO Prospectus
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa and P.R. Venkat
Private-equity firm TPG has filed a prospectus to list its Malaysia hospital assets, aiming to tap investor interest in a sector that has remained resilient amid heightened volatility.

A draft initial public offering prospectus filed with the Securities Commission Malaysia showed that Asia OneHealthcare plans to offer up to 4.38 billion shares. Of those, about 521 million will be new shares.
Asia OneHealthcare, or A1Health, is a private healthcare services provider backed by TPG and Malaysian conglomerate Hong Leong Group.

The institutional tranche of the offering is expected to comprise up to 3.76 billion shares offered to Malaysian and foreign investors at a price to be determined through a bookbuilding process, the prospectus showed.
Proceeds will be used to finance projects in line with the company's strategy to increase bed capacity and capabilities at hospitalsand develop new assets.

The Wall Street Journal previously reported details of the planned offering. If successful, the deal could be the third-largest in Malaysia, behind Petronas Chemicals' $4.14 billion IPO and a $3.1 billion offering by Felda Global Ventures, now known as FGV Holdings.

TPG and Hong Leong agreed to acquire Columbia Asia Healthcare, now known as A1Health, from Seattle-based Columbia Pacific Management for $1.2 billion in 2019. The operator was renamed in 2024 following the consolidation of healthcare assets across Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam.
Its portfolio includes more than 4,000 hospital beds in Southeast Asia, with most of its hospitals located in Malaysia.
U.S.-listed TPG is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, with $327 billion under management as of June 30.
